Alternatively, this meaning should be understood here. 'Greed' (`lobhaṃ`) means that for which greed is the cause; it is kamma caused by greed. So too with 'hatred.' Therefore it is said, 'With greed and hatred as the head, only kamma born of greed and hatred is indicated.' 'The cycle and the un-cycle' means the cycle and that which is not the cycle.

Nidānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Nidāna Sutta is completed.

5. Hatthakasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Hatthaka Sutta

35. Pañcame [V 2.0102] āḷaviyanti āḷaviraṭṭhe, na āḷavinagare. Tenāha “āḷaviyanti āḷaviraṭṭhe”ti. Athāti avicchedatthe nipāto. Tattha bhagavato nisajjāya avicchinnāya evāti attho. Tenāha “eva”ntiādi. Hatthato hatthaṃ gatattāti āḷavakassa yakkhassa hatthato sammāsambuddhassa hatthaṃ, tato rājapurisānaṃ hatthaṃ gatattā.

35. In the fifth, 'Āḷaviya' means in the country of Āḷavi, not in the city of Āḷavi. Therefore, it is said, 'Āḷaviya means in the country of Āḷavi.' 'Atha' is a particle in the sense of uninterruptedness. Here, the meaning is that the Blessed One’s sitting was indeed uninterrupted. Therefore, it is said, 'indeed,' and so on. 'Having gone from hand to hand' means from the hand of the yakkha Āḷavaka to the hand of the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, and from there to the hands of the king’s men.

Māghassāti māghamāsassa. Evaṃ phaggunassāti etthāpi. Khurantarehi kaddamo uggantvā tiṭṭhatīti kaddamo khurantarehi uggantvā tiṭṭhati. Catūhi disāhi vāyanto vāto verambhoti vuccati verambhavātasadisattā.

'Of Māgha' means of the month of Māgha. So too with 'of Phagguna.' 'Mud rises up between the hoofprints and remains' means mud rises up between the hoofprints and remains. Wind blowing from the four directions is called 'verambha' because of its similarity to the verambha wind.

Pañcadvārakāyanti pañcadvārānusārena pavattaṃ viññāṇakāyaṃ. Khobhayamānāti kilesakhobhavasena khobhayamānā cittaṃ saṅkhobhaṃ karontā. Cetasikāti manodvārikacittasannissitā. Tenāha “manodvāraṃ khobhayamānā”ti. So rāgoti taṃsadiso rāgo. Bhavati hi taṃsadise tabbohāro yathā “sā eva tittirikā, tāni eva osadhānī”ti. Yādiso hi ekassa puggalassa uppajjanakarāgo, tādiso eva tato aññassa rāgabhāvasāmaññato. Tena vuttaṃ “tathārūpo [M 2.0111] rāgo”tiādi. Icchitālābhena rajanīyesu vā niruddhesu vatthūsu domanassuppattiyā dosapariḷāhānaṃ sambhavo veditabbo.

'The body of five doors' means the aggregate of consciousness that occurs in accordance with the five sense doors. 'Agitating' means agitating the mind, causing disturbance, through the force of agitation by defilements. 'Mental states' refers to those dependent on the mind-door consciousness. Hence it is said, 'agitating the mind-door.' 'That lust' means lust similar to that. For there is usage of 'that' with similar things, just as 'the same partridge, the same medicinal herbs.' Indeed, the lust that arises for one person is similar to that of another due to the commonality in the nature of lust. Therefore, it is said, 'lust of such a kind,' and so on. The possibility of sorrow arising due to not obtaining desired things, or the burning of aversion due to the destruction of desirable objects, should be understood.

Na limpati anupalittacittattā. Sītibhūto nibbutasabbapariḷāhattā. Āsattiyo vuccanti taṇhāyo tattha tattha āsañjanaṭṭhena. Darathanti pariḷāhajātaṃ. Cetasoti sāmivacanaṃ.

He is not tainted because his mind is untainted. He is cooled, for all his burning distress is extinguished. Cravings are called 'attachments' because of their clinging in various places. 'Distress' refers to that which has arisen as burning. 'Of the mind' is a possessive term.

Hatthakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Hatthaka Sutta is completed.

6. Devadūtasuttavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Devadūta Sutta

36. Chaṭṭhe devadūtānīti liṅgavipallāsaṃ katvā vuttanti āha “devadūtā”ti, ubhayaliṅgaṃ vā etaṃ padaṃ, tasmā napuṃsakaliṅgavasena pāḷiyaṃ vuttassa pulliṅgavasena atthadassanaṃ kataṃ. Devoti maccūti abhibhavanaṭṭhena sattānaṃ attano vase vattāpanato maccurājā “devo”ti vuccati. Yathā hi devo pakatisatte abhibhavati, evaṃ maccu sabbasatte abhibhavati, tasmā devo [V 2.0103] viyāti devo. “Tassa dūtā”ti vatvā idānissa dūte tesaṃ dūtabhāvañca vibhāvetuṃ “jiṇṇabyādhimatā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tena codanatthena devassa dūtā viyāti devadūtāti dasseti. “Ahaṃ asukaṃ pamaddituṃ āgamissāmi, tuvaṃ tassa kese gahetvā mā vissajjehī”ti maccudevassa āṇākarā dūtā viyāti hi dūtāti vuccanti.

36. In the sixth, regarding devadūtāni, he says, ‘devadūtā,’ stating that it was spoken with an inversion of gender. Or, this word can be of both genders; therefore, although it is stated in the Pāli text in the neuter gender, the meaning is shown in the masculine gender. Deva means death. Because he overpowers beings and brings them under his control, the king of death is called a deva. For just as a god overpowers ordinary beings, so does death overpower all beings; therefore, he is like a god, thus a deva. Having said, ‘his messengers,’ now, to explain his messengers and their function as messengers, it is said, ‘the old, the sick, and the dead,’ and so on. By this, in the sense of prompting, it shows they are like the messengers of a god, hence devadūtā. For they are called messengers because they are like messengers who carry out the command of the god of death, which is: ‘I will come to crush so-and-so; you, seize him by the hair and do not release him.’

Idāni saddhātabbaṭṭhena devā viya dūtāti devadūtāti dassento “devā viya dūtā”tiādimāha. Tattha alaṅkatappaṭiyattāyāti idaṃ attano dibbānubhāvaṃ āvikatvā ṭhitāyāti dassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Devatāya byākaraṇasadisameva hoti na cirasseva jarābyādhimaraṇassa sambhavato. Visuddhidevānanti khīṇāsavabrahmānaṃ. Te hi carimabhave bodhisattānaṃ jiṇṇādibhedaṃ dassenti, tasmā antimabhavikabodhisattānaṃ visuddhidevehi upaṭṭhāpitabhāvaṃ upādāya tadaññesampi tehi anupaṭṭhāpitānampi tathā voharitabbatā pariyāyasiddhāti veditabbā. Disvāvāti [M 2.0112] visuddhidevehi dassite disvāva. Tatoyeva hi te visuddhidevānaṃ dūtā vuttā.

Now, showing that they are divine messengers in the sense of being trustworthy, he says, ‘like gods, messengers,’ and so on. Here, ‘adorned and prepared’ is said to show that they stand revealing their divine power. It is just like a deity’s prediction, for old age, sickness, and death will arise before long. ‘Of the pure gods’ means of the Arahant-Brahmās. For they show to Bodhisattas in their final existence the distinctions of old age and so on. Therefore, it should be understood that, because these signs are manifested for Bodhisattas in their last existence by pure gods, the same expression is conventionally established even for others for whom they are not so manifested. ‘Having seen’ means having seen what was shown by the pure gods. For that very reason they are called messengers of the pure gods.

Kasmā āraddhanti kevalaṃ devadūte eva sarūpato adassetvāti adhippāyo. Devānaṃ dūtānaṃ dassanūpāyattā tathā vuttanti dassento “devadūtā…pe… samanuyuñjatī”ti āha. Tattha devadūtā…pe… dassanatthanti devadūtānaṃ anuyuñjanaṭṭhānūpagassa kammassa dassanatthaṃ.

‘Why was this introduced?’ The intention is: why not just show the divine messengers in their true form? Showing that it was stated thus because it is a means for seeing the divine messengers, he said: ‘The divine messengers… he interrogates,’ and so on. Therein, ‘the divine messengers… for the purpose of showing’ means for the purpose of showing the kamma that leads to the state of being interrogated by the divine messengers.

Ekacce therāti andhakādike viññāṇavādino ca sandhāya vadati. Nerayike niraye pālenti tato niggantuṃ appadānavasena rakkhantīti nirayapālā. Atha vā nirayapālatāya nerayikānaṃ nirayadukkhena pariyonaddhāya alaṃ samatthāti nirayapālā. Tanti “natthi nirayapālā”ti vacanaṃ. Paṭisedhitamevāti “atthi nirayesu nirayapālā atthi ca kāraṇikā”tiādinā nayena abhidhamme (kathā. 866) paṭisedhitameva. Yadi nirayapālā nāma na siyuṃ, kammakāraṇāpi na bhaveyya. Sati hi kāraṇike kammakāraṇāya bhavitabbanti adhippāyo. Tenāha “yathā hī”tiādi. Etthāha – “kiṃ panete nirayapālā nerayikā, udāhu anerayikā”ti. Kiñcettha – yadi tāva nerayikā nirayasaṃvattaniyena kammena nibbattā, sayampi nirayadukkhaṃ paccanubhaveyyuṃ, tathā sati aññesaṃ nerayikānaṃ ghātanāya asamatthā siyuṃ, “ime nerayikā ime nirayapālā”ti vavatthānañca na siyā. Ye ca ye ghātenti, tehi samānarūpabalappamāṇehi itaresaṃ bhayasantāsā na siyuṃ. Atha anerayikā, nesaṃ tattha kathaṃ sambhavoti? Vuccate – anerayikā nirayapālā anirayagatisaṃvattaniyakammanibbattito. Nirayūpapattisaṃvattaniyakammato [V 2.0104] hi aññeneva kammunā te nibbattanti rakkhasajātikattā. Tathā hi vadanti sabbatthivādino –

‘Some elders’ refers to the Andhakas and others who are proponents of consciousness-only. They are ‘hell-wardens’ (nirayapālā) because they guard (pālenti) the hell-beings in hell, protecting it by not giving them a chance to escape. Or, they are ‘hell-wardens’ because they are fully capable with respect to the hell-beings who are enveloped by the suffering of hell. ‘That’ refers to the statement, ‘there are no hell-wardens.’ ‘It is refuted’ means it is indeed refuted in the Abhidhamma (Kvu 866) by the method beginning, ‘There are hell-wardens in the hells, and there are tormentors.’ If there were no such things as hell-wardens, there would also be no karmic causation of punishment. The intention is that if there is a tormentor, there must be the karmic causation of punishment. Therefore, he says, ‘just as,’ and so on. Here it is asked: ‘Are these hell-wardens hell-beings, or are they not hell-beings?’ And in this regard: if they were hell-beings, born from kamma that leads to hell, they themselves would experience the suffering of hell. In that case, they would be incapable of tormenting other hell-beings, and there would be no distinction such as, ‘these are hell-beings, these are hell-wardens.’ Moreover, the others would feel no fear or terror from those who torment them if they were of the same form, strength, and stature. But if they are not hell-beings, how do they come to exist there? It is said: The hell-wardens are not hell-beings, as they are born from kamma that leads to a non-hell destination. For they are born by a different kamma from that which leads to arising in hell, because they belong to the class of rākṣasas. Indeed, the Sarvāstivādins say—

“Kodhā kurūrakammantā, pāpābhirucino tathā;

Dukkhitesu ca nandanti, jāyanti yamarakkhasā”ti.

‘Those given to anger, who perform cruel deeds, and likewise delight in evil, and who rejoice in the afflicted, are born as Yama’s rākṣasas.’

Tattha yadeke vadanti “yātanādukkhaṃ paṭisaṃvedeyyuṃ, atha vā aññamaññaṃ ghāteyyu”ntiādi, tayidaṃ asāraṃ nirayapālānaṃ nerayikabhāvasseva [M 2.0113] abhāvato. Yadipi anerayikā nirayapālā, ayomayāya pana ādittāya sampajjalitāya sajotibhūtāya nirayabhūmiyā parikkamamānā kathaṃ dāhadukkhaṃ nānubhavantīti? Kammānubhāvato. Yathā hi iddhimanto cetovasippattā mahāmoggallānādayo nerayike anukampantā iddhibalena nirayabhūmiṃ upagatā dāhadukkhena na bādhīyanti, evaṃ sampadamidaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Therein, what some say, ‘They would experience the suffering of torment, or they would kill each other,’ and so on—this is baseless, because the hell-wardens lack the state of being a hell-being. Even if the hell-wardens are not hell-beings, how do they not experience the pain of burning while walking around on the iron ground of hell, which is blazing, thoroughly inflamed, and glowing? It is due to the power of kamma. For just as those with psychic power who have attained mastery of mind, like the great Moggallāna and others, out of compassion for hell-beings, go to the hell-realm by means of psychic power and are not afflicted by the pain of burning, so too should this matter be understood.

Iddhivisayassa acinteyyabhāvatoti ce? Idampi taṃsamānaṃ kammavipākassa acinteyyabhāvato. Tathārūpena hi kammunā te nibbattā yathā nirayadukkhena abādhitā eva hutvā nerayike ghātenti, na cettakena bāhiravisayābhāvo yujjati iṭṭhāniṭṭhatāya paccekaṃ dvārapurisesupi vibhattasabhāvattā. Tathā hi ekaccassa dvārassa purisassa ca iṭṭhaṃ ekaccassa aniṭṭhaṃ, ekaccassa ca aniṭṭhaṃ ekaccassa iṭṭhaṃ hoti. Evañca katvā yadeke vadanti “natthi kammavasena tejasā parūpatāpana”ntiādi, tadapāhataṃ hoti. Yaṃ pana vadanti “anerayikānaṃ tesaṃ kathaṃ tattha sambhavo”ti niraye nerayikānaṃ yātanāsabbhāvabhāvato. Nerayikasattayātanāyoggañhi attabhāvaṃ nibbattentaṃ kammaṃ tādisanikanti vināmitaṃ nirayaṭṭhāne eva nibbatteti. Te hi nerayikehi adhikatarabalārohapariṇāhā ativiya bhayānakadassanā kurūratarapayogā ca honti. Eteneva tattha nerayikānaṃ vibādhakakākasunakhādīnampi nibbattiyā atthibhāvo saṃvaṇṇitoti daṭṭhabbo.

If it is asked, ‘Is this because the sphere of psychic powers is incomprehensible?’ This too is similar, because the result of kamma is incomprehensible. For they are born by such kamma that they torment hell-beings while remaining unafflicted by the suffering of hell. Nor, on this account, is it logical to assume the non-existence of an external object, because pleasant and unpleasant natures are individually distinguished even among gatekeepers of the same gate. For what is pleasant for one gatekeeper is unpleasant for another, and what is unpleasant for one is pleasant for another. This being so, the claim of some, that ‘there is no tormenting of others by fire through the power of kamma,’ is refuted. As for what they say, ‘How can those who are not hell-beings exist there?’—it is because of the very existence of torment for hell-beings in hell. For the kamma that generates an individual existence suitable for the torment of hell-beings, being bent by such an inclination, produces it right in the location of hell. Indeed, compared to the hell-beings, they are of greater strength, height, and girth, are extremely terrifying in appearance, and employ even crueler methods. By this same reasoning, it should be understood that the existence of tormenting creatures like crows and dogs there is also explained.

Kathamaññagatikehi aññagatikabādhananti ca na vattabbaṃ aññatthāpi tathā dassanato. Yaṃ paneke vadanti “asattasabhāvā eva niraye nirayapālā niraye sunakhādayo cā”ti, tampetesaṃ matimattaṃ aññattha tathā adassanato. Na hi kāci atthi tādisī dhammappavatti, yā asattasabhāvā, sampatisattehi appayojitā ca atthakiccaṃ sādhentī diṭṭhapubbā. Petānaṃ pānīyanivārakānaṃ daṇḍādihatthānañca purisānaṃ sabbhāve asattabhāve ca visesakāraṇaṃ natthīti tādisānaṃ [V 2.0105] sabbhāve kiṃ pāpakānaṃ vattabbaṃ. Supinopaghātopi atthakiccasamatthatāya appamāṇaṃ dassanādimattenapi [M 2.0114] tadatthasiddhito. Tathā hi supine āhārūpabhogādinā na atthasiddhi, iddhinimmānarūpaṃ panettha laddhaparihāraṃ iddhivisayassa acinteyyabhāvato. Idhāpi kammavipākassa acinteyyabhāvatoti ce? Taṃ na, asiddhattā. Nerayikānaṃ kammavipāko nirayapālāti siddhamettaṃ, vuttanayena pāḷito ca tesaṃ sattabhāvo eva siddho. Sakkā hi vattuṃ sattasaṅkhātā nirayapālasaññitā dhammappavatti sābhisandhikaparūpaghāti atthakiccasabbhāvato ojāhārādi rakkhasasantati viya. Abhisandhipubbakatā cettha na sakkā paṭikkhipituṃ tathā tathā abhisandhiyā ghātanato. Tato eva na saṅghātapabbatehi anekantikatā. Ye pana vadanti “bhūtavisesā eva te vaṇṇasaṇṭhānādivisesavanto bheravākārā narakapālāti samaññaṃ labhantī”ti, tadasiddhaṃ ujukameva pāḷiyaṃ “atthi niraye nirayapālā”ti vādassa patiṭṭhāpitattā.

Nor should it be said, 'How can beings of one destiny obstruct those of another destiny?' for such is not seen elsewhere. As for what some say, 'The hell-wardens and hell-dogs in hell are not actual beings,' this is merely their opinion, as such is not seen elsewhere. For no such process of phenomena has ever been witnessed that is not an actual being and, without being employed by existing beings, accomplishes a purpose. There is no special reason to distinguish between the existence as beings and the non-existence as beings of the petas who obstruct water and the men with sticks in hand. Thus, given the existence of such beings, what is to be said of the evil ones? Harm in a dream is also not a valid measure for the ability to accomplish a purpose, because that purpose is accomplished by mere seeing and so on. For in a dream, there is no accomplishment of purpose through consuming food and so on. But a form created by psychic power is an exception here, due to the inconceivable nature of the sphere of psychic power. And if it is said, 'Is it not the same here, due to the inconceivable nature of karmic result?' That is not so, because it is unproven. It is established that the hell-wardens are the karmic result for the hell-beings, and by the method stated, their very nature as beings is also established. For it can be said: the process of phenomena designated as hell-wardens and counted as beings harms others with intention, due to the existence of a purpose, like a lineage of ogres who feed on vital essence. And here, the fact of its being preceded by intention cannot be rejected, because they harm in accordance with various intentions. For that very reason, there is no indeterminacy as with the crushing mountains. As for those who say, 'They are a special kind of spirit, possessing distinctions of color, shape, and so on, terrifying in appearance, who obtain the designation "hell-wardens,"' that is unproven, because the thesis, 'There are hell-wardens in hell,' is established straightforwardly in the Pāli itself.

Apica yathā ariyavinaye narakapālānaṃ bhūtamattatā asiddhā, tathā paññattimattavādinopi bhūtamattatā asiddhā sabbaso rūpadhammānaṃ atthibhāvasseva appaṭijānanato. Na hi tassa bhūtāni nāma paramatthato santi. Yadi paramatthaṃ gahetvā voharati, atha kasmā cakkhurūpādīni paṭikkhipatīti? Tiṭṭhatesā anavaṭṭhitatakkānaṃ appahīnavipallāsānaṃ vādavīmaṃsā. Evaṃ attheva niraye nirayapālāti niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ. Sati ca nesaṃ sabbhāve asatipi bāhire visaye narake viya desādiniyamo hotīti vādo na sijjhati, sati eva pana bāhire visaye desādiniyamoti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Moreover, just as in the Noble Discipline the mere-spirit-ness of hell-wardens is unproven, so too for one who holds they are mere concepts, their mere-spirit-ness is unproven, because they do not acknowledge the existence of material phenomena at all. For them, there are no such things as spirits in an ultimate sense. If they speak by taking the ultimate sense, then why do they reject visible forms and the like? Let this investigation of views be for those of unsettled reasoning, whose distortions are not abandoned. Thus, one should arrive at this conclusion: there are indeed hell-wardens in hell. And given their existence, the argument that there is regulation of place and so on, as in hell, even if external objects do not exist, does not succeed. However, it should be understood that there is regulation of place and so on only when external objects exist.

Devadūtasarāpanavasena satte yathūpacite puññakamme yameti niyametīti yamo. Tassa yamassa vemānikapetānaṃ rājabhāvato rañño. Tenāha “yamarājā nāma vemānikapetarājā”ti. Kammavipākanti akusalakammavipākaṃ. Vemānikapetā hi kaṇhasukkavasena missakaṃ kammaṃ katvā vinipātikadevatā viya sukkena kammunā paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhanti. Tathā hi maggaphalabhāginopi honti, pavattiyaṃ pana kammānurūpaṃ kadāci puññaphalaṃ, kadāci apuññaphalaṃ paccanubhavanti. Yesaṃ pana ariyamaggo uppajjati, tesaṃ maggādhigamato paṭṭhāya puññaphalameva uppajjatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Apuññaphalaṃ pubbe viya kaṭukaṃ na hoti, manussattabhāve ṭhitānaṃ [M 2.0115] viya mudukameva hotīti apare. Dhammiko rājāti ettha tassa dhammikabhāvo dhammadevaputtassa viya uppattiniyato dhammatāvasena veditabbo. Dvāresūti avīcimahānarakassa catūsu dvāresu. Khīṇāsavā brāhmaṇā nāma ukkaṭṭhaniddesena.

Because he reminds beings of the divine messengers and thus restrains and regulates them according to their accumulated wholesome kamma, he is called Yama. Due to his being the king of the Vemānika petas, he is a king. Hence it is said, 'Yamarāja is the king of the Vemānika petas.' 'Karmic result' means the result of unwholesome kamma. For Vemānika petas, having performed mixed kamma, dark and bright, take rebirth through bright kamma, like the deities in a state of downfall. Indeed, even those who are partakers of the path and fruit experience in the course of their existence sometimes the fruit of merit and sometimes the fruit of demerit, in accordance with their kamma. However, it should be understood that for those in whom the noble path arises, from the attainment of the path onward, only the fruit of merit arises. The fruit of demerit is not as bitter as before; it is mild, like for those established in a human existence—so say others. As for 'a righteous king,' his righteousness here should be understood as being determined by his birth, in accordance with the nature of things, like that of a Dhamma-devaputta. 'At the gates' means at the four gates of the great Avīci hell. 'Brahmins with cankers destroyed' is stated by way of the highest designation.

Anuyogavattanti [V 2.0106] anuyoge kate vattitabbavattaṃ. Āropentoti kārāpento, attano pucchaṃ uddissa paṭivacanaṃ dāpento pucchati. Parassa hi adhippāyaṃ ñātuṃ icchanto tadupagaṃ payogaṃ karonto pucchati nāma. Laddhinti gāhaṃ. Patiṭṭhāpentoti tattha niccakālaṃ kārāpento. Kāraṇaṃ pucchantoti yuttiṃ pucchanto. Samanubhāsatīti yathānuyuttamatthaṃ vibhūtaṃ katvā katheti.

Anuyogavatta means the duty to be performed when an inquiry is made. Āropento means causing to do; he asks, causing a reply to be given regarding his own question. For one who wishes to know another's intention is said to 'ask' when making an effort appropriate to that. Laddhi means a view. Patiṭṭhāpento means causing to be constantly established there. Kāraṇaṃ pucchanto means asking for the reason. Samanubhāsati means he speaks, having made the meaning clear and manifest according to what has been asked.

Jiṇṇanti jarāpattiyā jiṇṇaṃ. Ekacco daharakālato paṭṭhāya paṇḍurogādinā abhibhūtakāyatāya jiṇṇasadiso hoti, ayaṃ na tathā jarāpattiyā jiṇṇoti dasseti. Gopānasī viya vaṅkanti vaṅkagopānasī viya vaṅkaṃ. Na hi vaṅkabhāvassa nidassanatthaṃ avaṅkagopānasī gayhati. Bhagganti bhaggasarīraṃ kaṭiyaṃ bhaggakāyattā. Tenāha “imināpissa vaṅkabhāvameva dīpetī”ti. Daṇḍapaṭisaraṇanti ṭhānagamanesu daṇḍo paṭisaraṇaṃ etassāti daṇḍapaṭisaraṇaṃ tena vinā vattituṃ asamatthattā. Tenāha “daṇḍadutiya”nti. Jarāturanti jarāya patthatasaṃkilantakāyaṃ. Sabbaso kimihataṃ viya mahākhallāṭaṃ sīsamassāti mahākhallāṭasīsaṃ. Sañjātavalinti samantato jātavalikaṃ. Jarādhammoti jarāpakatiko. Tenāha “jarāsabhāvo”ti. Sabhāvo ca nāma tejodhātuyā uṇhatā viya na kadāci vigacchatīti āha “aparimutto jarāyā”tiādi.

Jiṇṇa means aged due to having reached old age. Some, from a young age, appear aged because their bodies are afflicted by conditions like jaundice; this shows that such a one is not aged by having reached old age. 'Bent like a rafter' means bent like a crooked rafter. For a straight rafter is not used to illustrate crookedness. Bhagga means broken-bodied, because the body is broken at the hip. Therefore, it is said, 'By this, he also reveals the state of crookedness.' Daṇḍapaṭisaraṇa means one for whom a staff is a refuge; for standing and walking, a staff is their refuge, as they are unable to manage without it. Therefore, it is said, 'with a staff as a companion.' Jarātura means one whose body is exhausted and wearied by old age. Mahākhallāṭasīsaṃ means one whose head is very bald, completely like a withered gourd. Sañjātavali means one on whom wrinkles have appeared all over. Jarādhamma means one who has the nature of aging. Therefore, it is said, 'the nature of aging.' And just as the heat of the fire element never departs, so it is said, 'not freed from aging,' and so on.

Atthato evaṃ vadati nāma, vācāya avadantopi atthāpattito evaṃ vadanto viya hoti viññūnanti attho. Taruṇo ahosiṃ yobbanena samannāgato. Ūrūnaṃ balaṃ etassa atthīti ūrubalī. Tena dūrepi gamanāgamanalaṅghanādisamatthataṃ dasseti, bāhubalīti pana iminā hatthehi kātabbakiccasamatthataṃ, javaggahaṇena vegasā pavattisamatthataṃ. Antarahitāti naṭṭhā. Ettha ca na kho panāhantiādi jarāya devadūtabhāvadassanaṃ. Tenāha “tenesa devadūto nāma jāto”ti. Ābādhassa [M 2.0116] atthitāya ābādhikaṃ. Vividhaṃ dukkhaṃ ādahatīti byādhi, visesena vā ādhiyati etenāti byādhi, byādhi saṃjāto etassāti byādhitaṃ. Esa nayo dukkhitanti etthāpi.

In meaning, he speaks thus; even if one does not speak with words, by implication he appears to speak thus to the wise—this is the meaning. 'I was young, endowed with youth.' Ūrubalī means one who has strength in the thighs. By that, it shows the ability to go far, return, leap, and so forth. By 'bāhubalī' (strong-armed), it indicates the ability to perform tasks with the hands; by the inclusion of 'java' (speed), the ability to proceed with speed. Antarahita means vanished, lost. And here, the passage beginning 'But I did not...' shows the nature of old age as a divine messenger. Therefore, it is said, 'Thus, this one has become the divine messenger.' Ābādhika means one who has an illness, due to the existence of illness. Byādhi (illness) is so called because it brings (ādahati) various kinds of suffering (dukkhaṃ), or because one is especially afflicted (ādhiyati) by it. Byādhita means one in whom illness (byādhi) has arisen (saṃjāto). This same method applies also to the word 'dukkhita' (suffering).

Dutiyaṃ devadūtanti etthāpi vuttanayeneva attho veditabbo. Byādhinā abhihatoti byādhinā bādhito, upaddutoti attho.

'The second divine messenger': here too, the meaning should be understood in the same way as explained. Byādhinā abhihato means struck by illness, that is, oppressed, assailed.

Viparibhinnavaṇṇoti viparibhinnanīlavaṇṇo. Tañhi yattha yattha gahitapubbakaṃ, tattha tattha paṇḍuvaṇṇaṃ, maṃsussadaṭṭhāne rattavaṇṇaṃ, yebhuyyena ca nīlasāṭakapārutaṃ viya hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “viparibhinnanīlavaṇṇo”ti.

Viparibhinnavaṇṇa means of discolored appearance, specifically of a discolored blue appearance. For wherever it was previously affected, there it is pale in color; at the places where flesh is swollen, it is red in color; and for the most part it is as if wrapped in a blue cloth. Therefore, it is said, 'of a discolored blue appearance.'

“Ko [V 2.0107] labhati, ko na labhatī”ti nirayupagasseva vasenāyaṃ vicāraṇāti “yena tāva bahu pāpaṃ kata”ntiādi āraddhaṃ. Bahu pāpaṃ katanti bahuso pāpaṃ kataṃ. Tena pāpassa bahulīkaraṇamāha. Bahūti vā mahantaṃ. Mahatthopi hi bahusaddo dissati “bahu vata kataṃ assā”tiādīsu, garukanti vuttaṃ hoti. So garukaṃ bahulaṃ vā pāpaṃ katvā ṭhito niraye nibbattatiyeva, na yamapurisehi yamassa santikaṃ nīyatīti. Parittanti pamāṇaparittatāya kālaparittatāya ca parittaṃ. Purimasmiṃ atthe agarūti attho, dutiyasmiṃ abahulanti. Yathāvuttamatthaṃ upamāya vibhāvetuṃ “yathā hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kattabbameva karontīti daṇḍameva karonti. Anuvijjitvāti vīmaṃsitvā. Vinicchayaṭṭhānanti aṭṭakaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ. Parittapāpakammāti dubbalapāpakammā. Attano dhammatāyāti parehi asāriyamānepi attano dhammatāya saranti. Te hi pāpakammassa dubbalabhāvato katūpacitassa ca okāsārahakusalakammassa balavabhāvato attano dhammatāyapi saranti. Sāriyamānāpīti “idaṃ nāma tayā kataṃ puññakamma”nti parehi sāriyamānāpi.

"Who gains, who does not gain?"—this consideration, with reference to those bound for hell, thus begins with "by whom much evil has been done," and so on. "Much evil has been done" means evil has been committed many times. By this, it refers to the multiplication of evil. Or, "much" can mean great. For the word 'bahu' is also seen in the sense of 'great,' as in "much indeed has been done by her," and so on; it means weighty. Having done weighty or abundant evil, one is reborn in hell itself; one is not led by Yama's men to Yama's presence. "Limited" means limited in measure and limited in time. In the first sense, it means 'not weighty'; in the second, 'not abundant.' To clarify the aforementioned meaning by means of a simile, "just as," and so on, is stated. "They do only what should be done" means they inflict punishment only. "Having investigated" means having examined. "The place of judgment" refers to the place of adjudication. "Those with limited evil deeds" means those whose evil deeds are weak. "By their own nature" means they remember by their own nature even when not reminded by others. For they, due to the weakness of their evil deeds and the strength of their accumulated wholesome deeds that are worthy of opportunity, remember even by their own nature. "Even when prompted" means even when reminded by others, as in "this wholesome deed was indeed done by you."

Ākāsacetiyanti girisikhare abbhokāse vivaṭaṅgaṇe katacetiyaṃ. Rattapaṭenāti rattavaṇṇena paṭena pūjesi paṭākaṃ katvā. Aggijālasaddanti paṭapaṭāyantaṃ narake aggijālasaddaṃ sutvāva. Attanā pūjitapaṭaṃ anussarīti tadā paṭākāya vātappahārasadde nimittassa gahitattā “mayā tadā ākāsacetiye pūjitarattapaṭasaddo viyā”ti attanā pūjitapaṭaṃ anussari.

"Celestial shrine" refers to a shrine built on a mountain peak, in an open space, with an open courtyard. "With a red cloth" means he worshipped it by making a banner with a red-colored cloth. "Sound of a fire-flame" refers to hearing the crackling sound of a fire-flame in hell. "He recalled the cloth he had offered" means that because the sound of the wind striking the banner was taken as a sign, he recalled the cloth he had offered, thinking, "It is just like the sound of the red cloth I offered at the celestial shrine at that time."

Sumanapupphakumbhenāti [M 2.0117] kumbhaparimāṇena sumanapuppharāsinā. “Dasādhikaṃ nāḷisahassakumbha”nti keci, “pañcaambaṇa”nti apare. Tīhipi na sarati balavato pāpakammena byāmohito. Tuṇhī ahosīti “kammāraho aya”nti tattha paṭikāraṃ apassanto tuṇhī ahosi.

"With a pot of jasmine flowers" means with a heap of jasmine flowers the size of a pot. Some say "a pot of a thousand and ten nāḷis," others say "five ambaṇas." Bewildered by his powerful evil kamma, he did not remember even these three. "He remained silent" means, seeing no remedy there and thinking, "This one is deserving of his kamma," he remained silent.

Ekapakkhacchadanamattāhīti majjhimappamāṇassa gehassa ekacchadanappamāṇehi. Suttāhataṃ karitvāti kāḷasuttaṃ pātetvā. Yathā ratho sabbaso pajjalito hoti ayomayo, evaṃ yugādayopissa pajjalitā sajotibhūtā eva hontīti āha “saddhiṃ…pe… rathe yojetvā”ti. Mahākūṭāgārappamāṇanti sattabhūmakamahākūṭāgārappamāṇaṃ.

"Just enough to cover one side of the roof" means the amount for one roof covering of a medium-sized house. "Having marked with a thread" means having stretched a black thread. Just as an iron chariot is completely ablaze, so too its yokes and other parts were ablaze and glowing—thus it is said, "together with... having yoked to the chariot." "The size of a great gabled house" means the size of a seven-storied great gabled house.

Vibhattoti sattānaṃ sādhāraṇena pāpakammunā vibhatto. Hīnaṃ kāyanti hīnaṃ sattanikāyaṃ, hīnaṃ vā attabhāvaṃ. Upādāneti catubbidhe upādāne. Atthato pana taṇhādiṭṭhiggāhoti āha “taṇhādiṭṭhiggahaṇe”ti[V 2.0108]. Sambhavati jarāmaraṇaṃ etenāti sambhavo, upādānanti āha “jātiyā ca maraṇassa cha kāraṇabhūte”ti. Anupādāti anupādāya. Tenāha “anupādiyitvā”ti. Sakalavaṭṭadukkhaṃ atikkantāti carimacittanirodhena vaṭṭadukkhassa kilesānampi asambhavato sabbaṃ vaṭṭadukkhaṃ atikkantā.

"Divided" means divided by the common evil kamma of beings. "Inferior body" refers to an inferior group of beings or an inferior state of existence. "Clinging" refers to the four kinds of clinging. But in meaning, it is grasping by craving and views—thus it is said, "in the grasping by craving and views." "From this, aging and death arise, thus it is an origin"—this is clinging; thus it is said, "the six causes of birth and of death." "Without clinging" means without clinging. Therefore, it is said, "without having clung." "Having transcended all the suffering of the cycle" means that with the cessation of the final consciousness, since there is no more arising of the suffering of the cycle and of the defilements, they have transcended all the suffering of the cycle.

Devadūtasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Devadūta Sutta is concluded.

7. Catumahārājasuttavaṇṇanā

7. The Commentary on the Catumahārāja Sutta

37. Sattame amā saha vattanti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ kicceti amaccā, sahitā. Parisati bhavāti pārisajjā, parivāraṭṭhāniyā parisāpariyāpannā. Tenāha “paricārikadevatā”ti. Tātāti ālapanaṃ. Evanti “kacci bahū manussā”tiādinā vuttākārena. Aṭṭha vāreti ekasmiṃ aḍḍhamāse catukkhattuṃ tathā itarasminti evaṃ aṭṭha vāre. Adhiṭṭhahantīti adhitiṭṭhanti. Paṭijāgarontīti paṭi paṭi jāgaronti. Puññaṃ karontā hi sattā jāgaronti nāma kātabbakiccappasutattā, itare pana supanti nāma sahitaparahitavimuttattā. Cātuddasiuposathassa anugamanaṃ viya pannarasiuposathassa paccuggamanaṃ na labbhati divasābhāvato.

37. In the seventh sutta, "ministers" means those who act together in each and every duty, being united. "Pārisajjā" means those who are in the assembly, those standing in the retinue, included in the assembly. Therefore, it is said, "attendant deities." "Tāta" is a term of address. "Thus" means in the manner stated, beginning with "Are there many people?" "Eight times" means four times in one half-month, and similarly in the other, thus eight times. "They resolve" means they stand firm. "They keep vigil" means they repeatedly stay awake. Beings who perform merit are indeed called "awake," because they are intent on the tasks to be done; the others, however, are called "asleep," because they are devoid of concern for their own and others' welfare. Just as the observance of the fourteenth-day Uposatha is followed, the welcoming of the fifteenth-day Uposatha is not obtained due to the absence of a day.

Tatoti [M 2.0118] tato tato. Taṃ upanissāyāti tā tā gāmanigamarājadhāniyo upanissāya. Adhivatthāti ārāmavanarukkhādīsu adhivatthā devatā. Teti te devā. Sandhāya kathetīti bhagavā katheti. Vuttanti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ.

"Tato" means "from there, from there." "Depending on that" means depending on those villages, market towns, and royal capitals. "Dwelling" refers to deities dwelling in monasteries, forests, trees, and so forth. "They" refers to those deities. "Speaks with reference to" means the Blessed One speaks. "Stated" means it is stated in the commentary.

Niccaṃ nibaddhaṃ uposatho saṃvacchare saṃvacchare paṭi paṭi haritabbato pavattetabbato pāṭihāriyapakkho nāma. Guṇaṅgehīti uposathaṅgehi.

Because the Uposatha must be constantly and regularly undertaken and carried out year after year, again and again, it is called the 'Pāṭihāriya-pakkha'.

Vutthavāsoti vusitabrahmacariyavāso. Kattabbakiccanti dukkhādīsu pariññātādikiccaṃ. Otāretvāti chaḍḍetvā. Parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanoti sabbaso khīṇabhavabandhano. Kāraṇena jānitvāti vipassanāpaññāsahitāya maggapaññāya cattāri ariyasaccāni jānitvā.

"One who has lived the holy life" means one who has dwelt in the completed holy life. "Duty to be done" refers to the task of full understanding, beginning with suffering, and so on. "Having discarded" means having abandoned. "One whose fetters of existence are exhausted" means one whose bonds of existence are entirely destroyed. "Knowing through reason" means knowing the Four Noble Truths with the wisdom of the path, accompanied by insight wisdom.

Jānantoti “arahantānaṃ anukaraṇappaṭipatti esā, yadidaṃ sammadeva uposathānuṭṭhāna”nti evaṃ uposathakammassa guṇaṃ jānanto. Evarūpenāti yādiso bhagavato uposathabhāvo vihito, evarūpena [V 2.0109] arahantānukaraṇena uposathakammena. Sakkā pahitatto vipassanaṃ ussukkāpetvā khīṇāsavasampattiṃ pāpuṇituṃ. Aṭṭhamaṃ uttānatthameva sattame vuttanayattā.

"Knowing" means understanding the virtue of the Uposatha observance, thinking, "This is the practice of emulating the arahants, namely, the proper undertaking of the Uposatha." "Of such a kind" means with an Uposatha observance of such a kind as that enacted by the Blessed One, emulating the arahants. It is possible for one who has applied himself to arouse insight and attain the accomplishment of the destruction of the taints. The eighth is straightforward in meaning, its meaning being as stated in the seventh.

Catumahārājasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Catumahārāja Sutta is finished.

9. Sukhumālasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Sukhumāla Sutta

39. Navame niddukkhoti kāyikacetasikadukkhavirahito. Sadukkhe hi savighāte sukhumālattā anavasarā, tasmā sukhito niddukkhatāya sukhumālo nāma. Yāvassa sukhumālattā paramukkaṃsagatāti āha “paramasukhumālo”ti. Ativiya sukhumāloti attho. Antamatītaṃ accantaṃ. Sabbadā sukhumāloti āha “satataniddukkho”ti. Cariyakāleti bodhicariyāya caraṇakāle. Tenāti bodhisattena. Aññattha pana padumanti rattaṃ kamalaṃ. Puṇḍarīkanti setaṃ vuccati. Itarāti itarapokkharaṇiyo. “Bodhisattassa kirā”tiādikaṃ pokkharaṇīnaṃ [M 2.0119] uppattidassanaṃ. Kuddālakammakāreti khaṇake. Pokkharaṇiṭṭhānānīti pokkharaṇikhaṇanayoggaṭṭhānāni. Gaṇhāpesīti khaṇāpesi. Pokkharaṇisaddo cettha tādise jalāsaye niruḷho daṭṭhabbo paṅkajādisaddā viya. Sopānabāhukānaṃ matthakaṭṭhānaṃ uṇhīsanti adhippetaṃ. Udakasecananāḷikāti udakacchaṭāvissajjananāḷiyantāni. Pañcavidhāti vaṇṇavasena jātivasena ca.

39. In the ninth sutta, "niddukkho" (free from suffering) means devoid of physical and mental suffering. For where there is suffering, there is vexation, and for the delicate, there is no opportunity for it. Therefore, being happy and free from suffering, he is called "delicate." Because his delicacy has reached the highest excellence, it is said, "paramasukhumālo" (supremely delicate). The meaning is "exceedingly delicate." "Accantaṃ" (exceedingly) means "antamatītaṃ" (having gone beyond the limit). Being always delicate, it is said, "satataniddukkho" (constantly free from suffering). "Cariyakāle" (during the period of practice) means during the time of practicing the Bodhisatta's conduct. "Tena" (by him) means by the Bodhisatta. Elsewhere, "paduma" refers to the red lotus. "Puṇḍarīka" is called the white lotus. "Itarā" (the others) refers to the other lotus ponds. The passage beginning "Bodhisattassa kirā" shows the origin of the ponds. "Kuddālakammakāra" (digger) means the excavator. "Pokkharaṇiṭṭhānāni" (the sites for the ponds) means the places suitable for digging ponds. "Gaṇhāpesi" (he had them taken) means he had them excavated. Here, the term "pokkharaṇī" should be understood as being conventionally established for such water reservoirs, like the terms "paṅkaja" and others. By "uṇhīsa" is meant the top part of the stair railings. "Udakasecananāḷikā" (water-sprinkling pipes) means the pipe mechanisms for releasing streams of water. "Pañcavidhā" (fivefold) means by way of color and by way of type.

Kho panassāti nipātamattaṃ. Kāsika-saddo ativiya saṇhe sukhume mahagghavatthe niruḷho, aññasmimpi tathājātike ruḷhivasena pavattatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tenāha “akāsikaṃ candana”nti. Hemante vāso hemantaṃ, hemantaṃ arahatīti hemantiko, pāsādo. “Itaresupi eseva nayo”ti vatvā tadeva nesaṃ arahataṃ dassetuṃ “tattha hemantiko”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sajālānīti sajālavātapānāni, udakayantānīti udakadhārāvissandanakayantāni. Pāsādamatthaketi pāsādassa upariākāsatale. Bandhitvāti payojitayante sukkhamahiṃsacammaṃ bandhitvā. Yantaṃ parivattetvāti yathāpayojitaṃ yantaṃ pāsāṇāropanatthañceva puna tesaṃ vissajjanatthañca parivattetvā. Tasmiṃ vissajjentīti chadanapiṭṭhe baddhasukkhamahiṃsacamme vissajjenti.

'Kho pana' is merely a particle. The term 'Kāsika' is conventionally established for very refined, delicate, and highly esteemed cloth, and it should be understood that it also applies to other things of similar nature by convention. Hence it is said, 'akāsikaṃ candana' (sandalwood not from Kāsī). 'Hemante vāso' (dwelling in winter) means winter; 'hemantiko' (suitable for winter) refers to a palace. Having stated, 'The same method applies to the others,' to show that these are suitable for them, it is said, 'therein, the winter dwelling,' and so on. 'Sajālāni' (with nets/lattices) means with latticed windows. 'Udakayantāni' (water machines) are machines that release streams of water. 'Pāsādamatthake' (on the palace top) means on the open space above the palace. 'Bandhitvā' (having fastened) means having fastened a dried buffalo hide to the machine that had been prepared. 'Yantaṃ parivattetvā' (turning the machine) means turning the machine as it was prepared, both for the purpose of raising stones and for releasing them again. 'Tasmiṃ vissajjenti' (releasing them there) means they release (the stones) onto the dried buffalo hide fastened on the roof covering.

Sahassathāmanti purisasahassabalaṃ, purisasahassena vahitabbabhāravahaṃ. Pallaṅke nisinnovāti ratanamayapallaṅke yathānisinno eva. Uppatanākārapattanti uppatitvā ṭhitaṃ viya. Jiyaṃ pothentassāti jiyāghātaṃ karontassa. Jiyappahārasaddoti jiyāghātasaddo. Yante baddhanti yantabaddhaṃ katvā [V 2.0110] ṭhapitaṃ. Saddantareti thāmamajjhimassa purisassa saddasavanaṭṭhāne. Gāvutassa catuttho bhāgo kosotipi vuccati dvisahassadaṇḍappamāṇaṭṭhānaṃ.

'Sahassathāma' (a thousand strong) means the strength of a thousand men, capable of bearing a load that a thousand men can carry. 'Pallaṅke nisinno' (seated on a couch) means seated on a jeweled couch just as one would sit. 'Uppatanākārapattanti' (having the appearance of one who has risen up) means appearing as if standing, having risen up. 'Jiyaṃ pothentassāti' (striking the bowstring) means making the bowstring resound. 'Jiyappahārasaddoti' (the sound of the bowstring being struck) means the sound of the bowstring being struck. 'Yante baddhanti' (bound to a machine) means having been fastened and placed on a machine. 'Saddantareti' (within earshot) refers to the place where the sound is heard by a man of middle strength. A quarter of a league is also called a 'kosa', a distance measuring two thousand rods.

Sabbaṭṭhānānīti mahāpurisassa tāni tāni sabbāni vasanaṭṭhānāni. Sikhābaddhoti purisasabhāvasseva visesato dassanametaṃ. Na uppilāvitabhāvatthanti uppilāvitabhāvasaṅkhātaṃ atthaṃ na kathesīti attho. Tassa hi bodhimūleyeva setughāto. Tenevāti appamādalakkhaṇassa [M 2.0120] dīpanato eva. Attānaṃ atikkamitvāti attano jarāpattiṃ acintetvā aṭṭīyati. Na panesa maggena pahīno tadā maggassa anadhigatattā. Sikkhaṃ paṭikkhipitvāti yathāsamādinnasikkhaṃ pahāya.

'Sabbaṭṭhānāni' (all places) refers to all those dwelling places of the Great Being. 'Sikhābaddho' (with a topknot) is specifically a description of the nature of a man. 'Na uppilāvitabhāvatthanti' (it does not convey the meaning of being boastful) means it does not speak of the state called 'boastfulness.' For him, the breaching of the dam occurs right at the root of enlightenment. 'Tenevāti' (therefore) means precisely because of the illumination of the characteristic of heedfulness. 'Attānaṃ atikkamitvāti' (having disregarded oneself) means he is distressed, not considering his own susceptibility to aging. But this was not abandoned by the path at that time, because the path had not yet been attained. 'Sikkhaṃ paṭikkhipitvāti' (having rejected the training) means by abandoning the training as undertaken.

Aviparītabyādhiādisabhāvāvāti ekantena byādhiādisabhāvā eva. Evaṃ jigucchāvihārenāti evaṃ sakalasseva vaṭṭadukkhassa jigucchanavihārena viharantassa. Evaṃ jigucchananti evaṃ parassa jigucchanaṃ. Paraṃ ajigucchamānoti karuṇāyanena evaṃ paraṃ ajigucchanto. Abhibhosmīti abhibhavitā asmi. Ussāho ahūti caturaṅgasamannāgataṃ vīriyameva catubbidhasammappadhānavīriyañca ahosi, yena maggabrahmacariyaparāyaṇo jāto.

'Aviparītabyādhiādisabhāvāvāti' (having a nature not contrary to disease, etc.) means having a nature entirely of disease and similar afflictions. 'Evaṃ jigucchāvihārenāti' (thus dwelling with disgust) means dwelling with disgust toward all the suffering of the cycle of existence. 'Evaṃ jigucchananti' (thus disgust) means disgust for another. 'Paraṃ ajigucchamānoti' (not feeling disgust toward another) means, through compassion, not feeling disgust toward another. 'Abhibhosmīti' (I am a conqueror) means 'I am an overcomer.' 'Ussāho ahūti' (effort arose) means the energy endowed with four factors arose, that is, the energy of the four kinds of right striving, through which one becomes devoted to the path and the holy life.

Sukhumālasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sukhumāla Sutta is concluded.

10. Ādhipateyyasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Ādhipateyya Sutta

40. Dasame abhibhavitvā pavattanaṭṭhena adhipati yaṃ kiñci jeṭṭhakaṃ na kārakaṃ attānaṃ adhipatīti katvā attā eva adhipati, tato āgataṃ attādhipateyyaṃ. Tenāha “attāna”ntiādi. Lokanti sattalokaṃ. So ca kho iddhividhādiguṇavisesayutto adhippeto adhipatibhāvassa adhippetattā. Navavidhaṃ lokuttaradhammanti ukkaṭṭhaniddesena vuttaṃ. Iti bhavoti evaṃ sampattibhavo, tattha evaṃ abhivuddhīti. Sampattibhavassa hetūti taṃtaṃsampattibhavassa tattha ca abhivuddhiyā hetu. Jātinimittassa kammabhavassa katūpacitattā jāti antopaviṭṭhā. Jarādīsupi eseva nayo hetusiddhiyā phalasiddhito.

40. In the tenth (sutta), 'adhipati' (overlord) means by way of proceeding having overcome; whatever is superior is not the doer. Considering oneself as the overlord, oneself is indeed the overlord. From that comes 'attādhipateyya' (self-overlordship). Hence it is said, 'attānaṃ' (oneself), and so on. 'Lokanti' (the world) means the world of beings. And that one is intended as endowed with special qualities such as psychic powers, since the state of overlordship is what is intended. 'Navavidhaṃ lokuttaradhammanti' (the ninefold supramundane Dhamma) is stated by way of an eminent designation. 'Iti bhavoti' (thus becoming) means such a state of attainment; therein, such growth. 'Sampattibhavassa hetūti' (the cause of the state of attainment) means the cause for that particular state of attainment and for growth therein. Because karmic becoming, the cause of rebirth, has been performed and accumulated, rebirth is included. The same method applies to aging, etc., because the fruit is established from the establishment of the cause.

Asallīnanti na saṅkocappattaṃ. Upaṭṭhitāti kāyādisabhāvasallakkhaṇavasena upaṭṭhitā. Asammuṭṭhā sammosābhāvato. Asāraddhoti sārambhassa sārambhahetūnañca vikkhambhanena asāraddho. Ekaggaṃ [V 2.0111] anekaggabhāvassa dūrasamussāpitattā. Nimmalaṃ katvāti rāgādimalānaṃ apanayanena malarahitaṃ katvā. Gopāyatīti saṃkilesānatthato rakkhati. Ayanti evaṃpaṭipanno bhikkhu. Suddhamattānaṃ pariharati asuddhabhāvassa kilesassapi abhāvato.

'Asallīnanti' (not withdrawn) means not having reached a state of contraction. 'Upaṭṭhitāti' (established) means being established through observation of the characteristics of the body and so on. 'Asammuṭṭhā' (not confused) means due to the absence of delusion. 'Asāraddhoti' (not agitated) means non-agitated due to the suppression of agitation and its causes. 'Ekaggaṃ' (one-pointed) means because the state of non-one-pointedness has been cast far away. 'Nimmalaṃ katvāti' (having purified) means having made it free from stains by removing the stains of lust and so on. 'Gopāyatīti' (he guards) means he protects from defilements and harm. 'Ayanti' (this one) refers to a bhikkhu who conducts himself in this way. He maintains himself pure because of the absence of the state of impurity, that is, of defilement.

Atikkamitvā [M 2.0121] maññasīti asakkhiṃ katvā maññasi. Tāya taṇhāya nibbattoti tammayo, taṇhāvasiko. Tassa bhāvo tammayatā, tassā tammayatāya abhāvena. Na hāyati paññādiguṇavepullappattiyā.

'Atikkamitvā maññasīti' (you think having transgressed) means 'you think having realized it.' 'Tāya taṇhāya nibbattoti' (produced from that craving) means 'tammayo' (consisting of that), under the power of craving. The state of that is 'tammayatā' (consisting of that); through the absence of that 'tammayatā', one does not decline in the attainment of an abundance of qualities like wisdom.

Ādhipateyyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Ādhipateyya Sutta is concluded.

Devadūtavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Devadūta Vagga is concluded.

5. Cūḷavaggo

5. The Minor Division

1. Sammukhībhāvasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Sammukhībhāva Sutta

41. Pañcamassa paṭhame sammukho bhavati yena so sammukhībhāvo, purato vijjamānatā, tasmā sammukhībhāvā. Puññakammanti dānasaṅkhātaṃ puññakammaṃ. Dve dhammā sulabhā bāhirattā yathāsakaṃ paccayasamavāyena labbhanato. Saddhā pana dullabhā pacurajanassa anavaṭṭhitakiccattā. Tenevāha “puthujjanassā”tiādi.

41. In the first [sutta] of the fifth [vagga], that by which one is face-to-face is 'sammukhībhāva', the state of being present, of existing in front; therefore, 'sammukhībhāvā' (from presence). 'Puññakammanti' (meritorious action) means meritorious action, namely, giving. Two things are easily obtained because they are external and obtainable by the coming together of their respective conditions. But faith is hard to obtain for many people because of their inconsistent duties. Therefore, he said, 'of an ordinary person,' and so on.

Sammukhībhāvasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sammukhībhāva Sutta is concluded.

2. Tiṭhānasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Tiṭhāna Sutta

42. Dutiye macchariyameva malaṃ macchariyamalaṃ, cittassa malīnasabhāvāpādanato vigataṃ macchariyamalaṃ etthāti vigatamacchariyamalaṃ. Gedhābhāvena koci kiñci dentopi tattha āsattiṃ na vissajjeti, ayaṃ pana na tādisoti āha “vissaṭṭhacāgo”ti. Malīnahatthova cittavisuddhiyā [V 2.0112] abhāvato. Dhotahatthova dhotahatthena kātabbakiccasādhanato. Tena vuttaṃ – “citte suddhe visujjhanti, iti vuttaṃ mahesinā”ti. Yācituṃ yutto yācakānaṃ manorathapūraṇato. Yācayogo payogāsahehi yācakehi suṭṭhu yuttabhāvato. Taṃsamaṅgī eva tattha rato nāma, na cittamattenevāti āha “dānaṃ…pe… rato nāma hotī”ti.

42. In the second [sutta], stinginess itself is the impurity—the impurity of stinginess. Because it produces an impure nature in the mind, 'one from whom the impurity of stinginess has departed' is so called because the impurity of stinginess has departed from him. Even if someone, out of greed, gives something, they do not relinquish attachment to it. But this one is not like that—hence he is called 'one of relinquished generosity.' He is like one with a soiled hand, due to the absence of mental purity. He is like one with a washed hand, because he accomplishes what should be done with a washed hand. Therefore it is said: 'When the mind is pure, they are purified—so declared the great sage.' He is worthy of being asked, because he fulfills the wishes of those who ask. He is fit to be asked, because he is very suitable for petitioners who have hope in their endeavor. Only one endowed with that is truly called 'one who delights therein'—not one who is so merely in mind. Hence it is said: 'He is called one who delights in giving...'

“Uccā, bhante”ti vatvā ayaṃ maṃ uccato vadatīti cinteyyāti puna “nātiuccā tumhe”ti āha, sarīrenāti adhippāyo. Mecakavaṇṇassāti nīlobhāsassa. Pucchīti bhikkhū pucchi. Bhūmiyaṃ lekhaṃ likhanto acchīti paṭhamaṃ [M 2.0122] mañce nipajjitvā uṭṭhāya bhūmiyaṃ lekhaṃ likhanto acchi “akhīṇāsavoti maññanā hotū”ti. Tathā hi rājā khīṇāsavassa nāma…pe… nivatti. Dhajapaggahitāvāti paggahitadhajāva. Silācetiyaṭṭhānanti thūpārāmassa ca mahācetiyassa ca antare silāya katacetiyaṭṭhānaṃ. Cetiyaṃ…pe… aṭṭhāsi sāvakassa taṃ kūṭāgāranti katvā.

Having said, 'High, sir,' lest he think, 'This one speaks to me from a high position,' he said again, 'You are not too high,' meaning in body. 'Of Mecakavaṇṇa' means of a blue luster. 'He asked' means he asked a bhikkhu. 'He was drawing a line on the ground' means first he lay down on the couch, then, having risen, he was drawing a line on the ground, thinking, 'Let there be the perception that I am one whose taints are not destroyed.' For indeed, the king... returned. 'With banners raised' means like raised flags. 'The stone shrine’s place' means the site of a shrine made of stone between the Thūpārāma and the Great Shrine. The shrine... stood, having been made into that disciple’s peaked dwelling.

Pacchābhāgenāti dhammakathikassa therassa piṭṭhipassena. Gonasoti maṇḍalasappo. Dhammassavanantarāya bahūnaṃ saggamaggappaṭilābhantarāyo bhaveyyāti adhippāyena “dhammassavanantarāyaṃ na karissāmī”ti cintesi. Visaṃ vikkhambhetvāti vipassanātejena visavegaṃ vikkhambhetvā. Gāthāsahassanti gāthāsahassavantaṃ. Paṭṭhānagāthāyāti paṭṭhāpanagāthāya, ādigāthāyāti attho. Paṭṭhāna…pe… avasānagāthaṃ eva vavatthapesi, na dvinnaṃ antare vuttaṃ kilantakāyattā. Sarabhāṇaṃ sāyanhadhammakathā. Paggaṇhātīti paccakkhaṃ karontī gaṇhāti, sakkaccaṃ suṇātīti attho. Dhammakathanadivase dhammakathikānaṃ akilamanatthaṃ saddhā upāsakā siniddhabhojanaṃ madhupānakañca denti sarassa madhurabhāvāya sappimadhukatelādiñca bhesajjaṃ. Tenāha “ariyavaṃsaṃ kathessāmī”tiādi. Catūhi dāṭhāhi ḍaṃsitvāti daḷhadaṭṭhabhāvadassanaṃ. Carissāmīti sammānessāmi, sakkaccaṃ suṇissāmīti attho. Nimmathetvāti nimmadditvā, apanetvāti attho.

'Pacchābhāgena' means behind the back of the elder who teaches the Dhamma. 'Gonasoti' refers to a maṇḍalasappo cobra. With the intention that an obstacle to hearing the Dhamma would be an obstacle for many to attaining the path to heaven, he thought, 'I will not create an obstacle to hearing the Dhamma.' 'Visaṃ vikkhambhetvāti' means suppressing the venom's force through the power of insight. 'Gāthāsahassanti' refers to one who possesses a thousand verses. 'Paṭṭhānagāthāyāti' means the paṭṭhāpana introductory verse, the first verse. He established the beginning...pe...and concluding verses but did not speak between them due to bodily fatigue. 'Sarabhāṇaṃ' refers to the evening Dhamma discussion. 'Paggaṇhātīti' means one takes it up directly, perceiving, listening attentively. On the day of the Dhamma discourse, devout lay followers offer rich food, honey drinks, and medicinal remedies like ghee, honey, and oil to the Dhamma teachers to prevent fatigue and to enhance the sweetness of the voice. Hence it is said, 'I will speak of the noble lineage,' etc. 'Catūhi dāṭhāhi ḍaṃsitvāti' demonstrates the firmness of the bite with four fangs. 'Carissāmīti' means 'I will honor it,' that is, 'I will listen carefully.' 'Nimmathetvāti' means having crushed and removed it.

Tiṭhānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Tiṭhānasutta is completed.

3. Atthavasasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Atthavasasutta

43. Tatiye attho nāma phalaṃ, taṃ etassa vasoti atthavaso. Hetu, attho etassa atthīti attho, so evāti āha “tayo atthe tīṇi kāraṇānī”ti. Dhammadesanā nāma ukkaṭṭhaniddesena [V 2.0113] catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ pakāsanāti āha “catusaccadhammaṃ pakāsetī”ti. Aṭṭhakathaṃ ñāṇena paṭisaṃvedīti pāḷipadānaṃ atthaṃ vivaraṇañāṇena paṭi paṭi saṃvedanasīlo “ayaṃ imassa bhāsitassa attho”ti. Etena atthapaṭisambhidābyāpāramāha. Pāḷidhammaṃ paṭisaṃvedīti pāḷigatiṃ pāḷiṃ padavivaraṇaṃ paṭi paṭi saṃvedanasīlo. Etena dhammapaṭisambhidābyāpāramāha.

43. In the third sutta, 'attha' means fruit; because it is under its sway (vasa), it is 'atthavasa.' A cause, a meaning, is present in it, thus it is 'attha.' That is why it is said: 'Three meanings, three reasons.' The teaching of the Dhamma refers to the exposition of the Four Noble Truths through supreme explanation; hence it is said: 'He expounds the Dhamma of the Four Truths.' 'He comprehends the meaning with knowledge' means he is of the nature of repeatedly understanding the meaning of the Pāli terms with the knowledge of explanation, thinking, 'This is the meaning of this statement.' By this is stated the function of the analytical knowledge of meaning. 'He comprehends the Pāli Dhamma' means he is of the nature of repeatedly understanding the Pāli style, the Pāli text, and the explanation of the terms. By this is stated the function of the analytical knowledge of the Dhamma.

Atthavasasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Atthavasasutta is completed.

4. Kathāpavattisuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Kathāpavattisutta

44. Catutthe [M 2.0123] pavattinīti yāva adhippetatthanigamanā avicchedena pavattinī. Paṭighātābhāvena appaṭihatā. Niyyānikā sappāṭihīrakā.

44. In the fourth sutta, 'pavattinī' means that which proceeds uninterruptedly until the conclusion of the intended meaning. It is unimpeded due to the absence of obstruction. It is emancipating and miraculous.

Kathāpavattisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kathāpavattisutta is completed.

5. Paṇḍitasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Paṇḍitasutta

45. Pañcame paṇḍitapaññattānīti paṇḍitehi paṭhamaṃ paññattāni. Kathitānīti seyyaso kathitāni. Mahāpurisehīti buddhabodhisattehi. Karuṇāti karuṇācetovimutti vuttā. Pubbabhāgoti tassa upacāro. Damoti indriyasaṃvaro “manacchaṭṭhānaṃ indriyānaṃ damana”nti katvā. Attadamananti cittadamanaṃ. Puṇṇovāde (ma. ni. 3.396) “sakkhissasi kho, tvaṃ puṇṇa, iminā damūpasamenā”ti āgatattā damoti vuttā khantipi. Āḷavake āḷavakasutte (saṃ. ni. 1.246; su. ni. 190) “saccā damā cāgā”ti evaṃ vuttā paññāpi imasmiṃ sutte “damo”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Rakkhanaṃ gopanaṃ paṭijaggananti mātāpitūnaṃ manussāmanussakatūpaddavato rakkhanaṃ, byādhiādianatthato gopanaṃ, ghāsacchādanādīhi veyyāvaccakaraṇena paṭijagganaṃ. Santo nāma sabbakilesadarathapariḷāhūpasamena upasantakāyavacīsamācāratāya ca. Uttamaṭṭhena santānanti matteyyatādīhi seṭṭhaṭṭhena santānaṃ.

45. In the fifth sutta, 'paṇḍitapaññattāni' means what was first established by the wise. 'Kathitāni' means what was excellently spoken. 'Mahāpurisehi' means by the Buddhas and Bodhisattas. 'Karuṇā' refers to the liberation of mind through compassion. 'Pubbabhāgo' is its preliminary stage. 'Damo' means restraint of the faculties, in the sense of 'the taming of the six faculties with the mind as the sixth.' 'Attadamanaṃ' means taming of the mind. In the Puṇṇovāda (MN 145), since it is stated, 'You, Puṇṇa, will be able to endure with this taming and calming,' patience is also called 'damo.' In the Āḷavaka Sutta (SN 10.12; Sn 1.10), since it is stated, 'truth, taming, generosity,' it is also fitting in this sutta to call wisdom 'damo.' 'Rakkhanaṃ, gopanaṃ, paṭijagganaṃ' means protecting one's parents from dangers caused by humans and non-humans, guarding them from misfortunes such as illness, and attending to them by performing services such as providing food and clothing. 'Santo' refers to those who are peaceful due to the calming of all defilements, distress, and burning, and due to their tranquil bodily and verbal conduct. 'Uttamaṭṭhena santānaṃ' means peaceful in the highest sense, that is, peaceful in the sense of being supreme due to qualities such as reverence for one's mother.

Idha imesaṃyeva tiṇṇaṃ ṭhānānaṃ karaṇenāti imasmiṃ sutte āgatānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ ṭhānānaṃ karaṇena nibbattanena. Etāni…pe… kāraṇānīti mātupaṭṭhānaṃ pitupaṭṭhānanti etāni dve uttamapurisānaṃ [V 2.0114] kāraṇāni. Uttamakiccakaraṇena hi mātāpituupaṭṭhākā “uttamapurisā”ti vuttā. Tenāha “mātāpitu…pe… vutto”ti. Anupaddavabhāvena khemaṃ.

Here, 'by the doing of these three things' means by the accomplishment and production of the three things mentioned in this sutta. 'These… causes' means serving one’s mother and serving one’s father—these two are causes for supreme persons. Indeed, those who serve their parents by performing the highest duties are called 'supreme persons' (uttamapurisā). Therefore, it is said, 'mother and father… is spoken of.' 'Khemaṃ' means security through the state of being without affliction.

Paṇḍitasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Paṇḍitasutta is completed.

6. Sīlavantasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Sīlavantasutta

46. Chaṭṭhe [M 2.0124] lokiyalokuttaramissakanti ettha “manussā puññaṃ pasavantī”ti avisesena vuttattā bhāvanāmayassapi puññassa saṅgaṇhanato lokuttarassapi sambhavo daṭṭhabbo.

46. In the sixth sutta, regarding 'mixed worldly and supramundane,' because it is stated without specification that 'humans generate merit,' it should be understood that the supramundane is also possible, since this includes merit consisting of mental development.

Sīlavantasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Sīlavantasutta is completed.

7. Saṅkhatalakkhaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Saṅkhatalakkhaṇasutta

47. Sattame samecca sambhūya paccayehi kataṃ saṅkhataṃ. Nimittānīti sañjānanassa nimittāni. Hetupaccayasamavāye uppajjanaṃ uppādo, attalābho. Vayoti bhaṅgo. Ṭhitassāti uppādakkhaṇato uddhaṃ ṭhitikkhaṇapattassa. Sā panassa avatthā uppādāvatthāya bhinnāti katvā aññathattaṃ jarāti ca vuttā. Yasmā dhammo uppajjamāno eva bhijjati, tathā sati uppādabhaṅgā samānakkhaṇā siyuṃ, na ca taṃ yujjati, tasmā uppādāvatthāya bhinnā bhaṅgābhimukhāvatthā jarāti veditabbā. Ye pana “saṅkhārānaṃ ṭhiti natthī”ti vadanti, tesaṃ taṃ micchā. Yathā hi tasseva dhammassa uppādāvatthāya bhinnā bhaṅgāvatthā icchitā, aññathā “aññaṃ uppajjati, aññaṃ nirujjhatī”ti āpajjati, evaṃ uppajjamānassa bhaṅgābhimukhā dhammā icchitabbā. Sā ca ṭhitikkhaṇo. Na hi uppajjamāno bhijjatīti sakkā viññātunti.

47. In the seventh sutta, the conditioned is that which is made by conditions, having come together and arisen together. 'Nimittāni' are the signs of cognition. Arising (uppādo) is coming into being through the conjunction of causes and conditions, the acquisition of existence. Passing away (vayo) is dissolution. 'Of what persists' (ṭhitassa) refers to that which has reached the moment of persistence after the moment of arising. That state is distinct from the state of arising, and thus it is called alteration and aging. If a phenomenon were to break apart just as it arises, then arising and dissolution would occur in the same moment, which is not logical. Therefore, the state facing dissolution, which is distinct from the state of arising, is to be understood as aging. Those who say, 'There is no persistence of conditioned things,' are wrong. For just as the state of dissolution of that very phenomenon is accepted as distinct from the state of arising—otherwise, it would follow that 'one thing arises, another ceases'—so too, a state facing dissolution must be accepted for that which is arising. And that is the moment of persistence. For it cannot be understood that what is arising is also breaking apart.

Saṅkhatanti tebhūmakā dhammā paccayasamuppannattā. Yadi evaṃ maggaphaladhammā kathanti āha “maggaphalāni panā”tiādi. Lakkhaṇakathā hi yāvadeva sammasanatthā. Uppādakkhaṇe uppādo, na ṭhānabhaṅgakkhaṇesu. Kasmā? Uppādauppādakkhaṇānaṃ aññamaññaṃ paricchinnattā. Yathā hi uppādasaṅkhātena vikārena uppādakkhaṇo paricchinno, evaṃ uppādakkhaṇenapi uppādo paricchinno. Sesadvayepi eseva nayo. Dhammappavattimattatāyapi kālassa lokasamaññāvaseneva vuttaṃ. Lakkhaṇaṃ na saṅkhataṃ, saṅkhataṃ na lakkhaṇanti nesaṃ bhedadassanaṃ. Avatthāvato hi avatthā bhinnāvāti[V 2.0115]. Paricchinnanti ettha uppādavayehi tāva saṅkhataṃ paricchinnaṃ hotu, jarāya pana taṃ kathaṃ paricchinnanti vuccati? Na vuccati paricchedo pubbantāparantamattena, atha kho sabhāvabhedenāti nāyaṃ doso. Saṅkhataṃ dhammajātaṃ paricchinnaṃ tabbantaṃ dhammajātaṃ [M 2.0125] saṅkhatanti paññāyati evaṃ tesaṃ abhāvena nibbānametanti lakkhitabbato sañjānitabbato. Idāni “yathā hī”tiādinā yathāvuttamattaṃ upamāhi vibhāveti.

'Conditioned' (saṅkhata) refers to the phenomena of the three realms because they are dependently arisen. If so, what about the path and fruition states? He says, 'But the path and fruition states,' and so on. The discussion of characteristics is solely for the purpose of comprehension. Arising occurs at the moment of arising, not at the moments of persistence or dissolution. Why? Because arising and the moment of arising are mutually defined. Just as the moment of arising is defined by the change designated as arising, so too arising is defined by the moment of arising. The same principle applies to the other two. Even regarding the mere occurrence of phenomena, time is spoken of by way of worldly convention. The characteristic is not the conditioned; the conditioned is not the characteristic—thus their difference is shown. For a state is distinct from that which possesses the state. Regarding 'defined': let the conditioned be defined by arising and passing away, but how is it said to be defined by aging? Definition is not spoken of merely by a beginning and an end, but rather by a distinction of nature; thus, there is no fault here. The conditioned class of phenomena is defined; that class of phenomena is known as conditioned. Thus, Nibbāna is to be marked and cognized as such due to the absence of these characteristics. Now, with 'just as,' and so on, he clarifies what has been said by means of similes.

Saṅkhatalakkhaṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Saṅkhatalakkhaṇasutta is completed.

8. Asaṅkhatalakkhaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Asaṅkhatalakkhaṇasutta

48. Aṭṭhame asaṅkhatassāti vuttanayena na saṅkhatassa. Tenāha “paccayehī”tiādi. Yathā uppādādīnaṃ bhāvena saṅkhatadhammajātaṃ saṅkhatanti paññāyati, evaṃ tesaṃ abhāvena nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti paññāyati.

48. In the eighth, 'of the unconditioned' means, in the manner previously stated, not of the conditioned. Therefore, it is said, "by conditions," etc. Just as the collection of conditioned phenomena is known as conditioned due to the presence of arising, etc., so too, Nibbāna is known as unconditioned due to the absence of these.

Asaṅkhatalakkhaṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Asaṅkhatalakkhaṇa Sutta is concluded.

9. Pabbatarājasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Pabbatarāja Sutta

49. Navame idha sāla-saddo rukkhasāmaññapariyāyo, na rukkhavisesapariyāyoti āha “mahāsālāti mahārukkhā”ti. Kulajeṭṭhakanti tasmiṃ kule jeṭṭhabhūtaṃ sāmibhūtaṃ. Silāmayo na paṃsumayo missako ca. Gāmaṃ gāmūpacārañca ṭhapetvā sabbaṃ araññanti āha “araññasminti agāmakaṭṭhāne”ti. Mahanto pabbato seloti yojanā.

49. In the ninth, here the word "sāla" is a general term for trees, not a specific type of tree; hence it is said, "mahāsālā means great trees." "Chief of the clan" means the one who has become the eldest, the master, in that family. "Made of stone, not of earth, and not mixed." "Except for the village and its environs, all is wilderness," hence it is said, "in the wilderness means in a place without a village." The construction is: "a great mountain of rock."

Pabbatarājasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Pabbatarāja Sutta is concluded.

10. Ātappakaraṇīyasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Ātappakaraṇīya Sutta

50. Dasame sarīrasambhavānanti sarīre sambhūtānaṃ. Dukkhānanti aniṭṭhānaṃ. Bahalānanti nirantarappavattiyā aviraḷānaṃ. Tāpanavasenāti dukkhāpanavasena. Tibbānanti kurūrānaṃ. Tāsaṃ yathāvuttānaṃ adhivāsanāya pahātabbadukkhavedanānaṃ pajahanaṃ nāma khamanamevāti āha “khamanatthāyā”ti[V 2.0116]. Āṇāpetvāti “ātappaṃ karaṇīya”nti buddhāṇaṃ vidhāya. Lokiyalokuttaramissakā kathitā sasambhārānaṃ maggadhammānaṃ kathitattā.

50. In the tenth, "arising in the body" means of those that have arisen in the body. "Of sufferings" means of the undesirable. "Dense" means unbroken due to continuous occurrence. "By way of tormenting" means by way of causing suffering. "Severe" means of the harsh. "For the endurance of these as described" means that the abandonment of painful feelings that ought to be abandoned is forbearance itself; hence he said, "for the sake of endurance." "Having commanded" means having enjoined the Buddhas' command, 'Ardor should be made.' The discussion is a mixture of mundane and supramundane, since the path-dhammas together with their requisites are discussed.

Ātappakaraṇīyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Ātappakaraṇīya Sutta is concluded.

11. Mahācorasuttavaṇṇanā

11. Commentary on the Mahācora Sutta

51. Ekādasame [M 2.0126] mahābalavacoro mahācoroti āha “mahanto balavacoro”ti. Balavacoroti ca mahāthāmatāya mahāparivāratāya mahācoriyakammasamatthatāya ca veditabbo. Mahataṃ gāmanigamānaṃ viluppanaṃ mahāvilopo. Taṃ taṃ kāraṇaṃ pakkhipitvāti taṃ taṃ akaraṇameva kāraṇaṃ katvā tappaṭibaddhāya kathāya pakkhipitvā. Atthaṃ kathayissantīti tassa tassa atthañca kathayissanti. Harantāti apanentā pariharantā. Dasavatthukāyāti “sassato loko”ti (ma. ni. 1.269) ādidasavatthusannissitāya. Antaṃ gahetvā ṭhitadiṭṭhiyāti tameva sassatādiantaṃ gahetvā avissajjetvā ṭhitadiṭṭhiyā.

51. In the eleventh, a 'great thief' (mahācora) is a very powerful thief; hence it is said, "a great and powerful thief." A "powerful thief" should be understood as being someone with great strength, a large retinue, and the capacity for committing great acts of theft. "The plundering of large villages and towns is great plunder." "Having inserted this or that cause" means making even a non-cause a cause, and inserting it into the discussion related to that. "They will explain the meaning" means they will explain the meaning of this or that. "Taking away" means removing, carrying away. "Based on ten grounds" means based on the ten grounds beginning with "the world is eternal," etc. "With a view fixed on an extreme" means with a view that holds firmly to that very eternalist or other extreme, without relinquishing it.

Mahācorasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Mahācora Sutta is concluded.

Cūḷavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Cūḷavagga is concluded.

Paṭhamapaṇṇāsakaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The First Fifty is concluded.

2. Dutiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ

2. The Second Fifty

(6) 1. Brāhmaṇavaggo

(6) 1. The Brāhmaṇa Chapter

1. Paṭhamadvebrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the First Two Brāhmaṇa Suttas

52. Brāhmaṇavaggassa [M 2.0127][V 2.0117] paṭhame jarājiṇṇāti jarāvasena jiṇṇā, na byādhiādīnaṃ vasena jiṇṇasadisattā jiṇṇā. Vayovuddhāti vayaso vuddhippattiyā vuddhā, na sīlādivuddhiyā. Jātimahallakāti jātiyā mahantatāya cirarattaññutāya jātimahallakā. Tayo addhe atikkantāti paṭhamo, majjhimo, pacchimoti tayo addhe atītā. Tatiyaṃ vayaṃ anuppattāti tato eva pacchimaṃ vayaṃ anuppattā. Akatabhayaparittāṇāti ettha bhayaparittāṇanti duggatibhayato parittāyakaṃ puññaṃ, taṃ akataṃ etehīti akatabhayaparittāṇā. Patiṭṭhākammanti sugatisaṅkhātappatiṭṭhāvahaṃ kammaṃ. Upasaṃharīyatīti sampāpīyati. “Upanīyatī”ti vuttaṃ, kiṃ kena upanīyatīti āha “ayañhi jātiyā jaraṃ upanīyatī”tiādi. Ayanti loko. Jāto na jātabhāveneva tiṭṭhati, atha kho tato paraṃ jaraṃ pāpīyati, jarāya byādhiṃ pāpīyati. Evaṃ parato paraṃ dukkhameva upanīyati.

52. In the first of the Brāhmaṇa Chapter, "worn by old age" means worn out by the power of aging, not worn out by being like one worn out by illness or other causes. "Advanced in years" means advanced by the progression of age, not by growth in virtue or other qualities. "Ancient by birth" means ancient due to greatness of birth and long-standing experience. "Having passed the three stages" refers to having passed the first, middle, and last stages. "Having reached the third age" means having for that reason reached the final age. "Without having made a refuge from fear" means not having done meritorious deeds that are a refuge from the fear of a bad destination. "The act of establishing" refers to the action bringing about the establishment known as a fortunate rebirth. "Is brought near" means it is made to reach. It is said, "It is brought near," but what is brought near by what? He said, "For this birth brings aging near," and so on. "This" refers to the world. One who is born does not remain merely in the state of birth, but rather proceeds to aging, and through aging, to sickness. Thus, from one to the next, suffering itself is brought near.

Tāyanaṭṭhenāti rakkhanaṭṭhena. Nilīyanaṭṭhenāti nilīnaṭṭhānabhāvena. Patiṭṭhānaṭṭhenāti patiṭṭhānabhāvena. Avassayanaṭṭhenāti avassayitabbabhāvena. Uttamagativasenāti paramagatibhāvena.

By the meaning of 'protecting,' it means 'guarding.' By the meaning of 'hiding,' it means 'being a place of hiding.' By the meaning of 'support,' it means 'being a foundation.' By the meaning of 'reliance,' it means 'being that which should be relied upon.' By way of being the 'ultimate destination,' it means 'being the supreme destination.'

Paṭhamadvebrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the First Two Brāhmaṇa Suttas is concluded.

2. Dutiyadvebrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Second Two Brāhmaṇa Suttas

53. Dutiye bhajitabbaṭṭhena paresaṃ bhājitabbaṭṭhena bhājanaṃ, bhaṇḍakaṃ.

53. In the second, a 'vessel' (bhājanaṃ), a 'utensil' (bhaṇḍakaṃ), is so called by the meaning of being divided or by the meaning of being distributed among others.

Dutiyadvebrāhmaṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Two Brāhmaṇa Suttas is concluded.

3-4. Aññatarabrāhmaṇasuttādivaṇṇanā

3-4. Commentary on the Aññatarabrāhmaṇa Sutta and Others

54-55. Tatiye [V 2.0118][M 2.0128] yesaṃ rāgādīnaṃ appahānena purisassa attabyābādhādīnaṃ sambhavo, pahānena asambhavoti evaṃ rāgādīnaṃ pahāyako ariyadhammo mahānubhāvatāya mahānisaṃsatāya ca sāmaṃ passitabboti sandiṭṭhiko. Iminā nayena sesesu padesupi yathārahaṃ nīharitvā vattabbo. Saddattho pana visuddhimaggasaṃvaṇṇanāsu (visuddhi. mahāṭī. 1.147) vuttanayena veditabbo. Catutthaṃ uttānatthameva.

54-55. In the third, for a person for whom lust and other defilements are not abandoned, there is the arising of harm to oneself and so forth; but when they are abandoned, such harm does not arise. Thus, the noble Dhamma, being the abandoner of lust and so forth, is to be seen by oneself, being of great power and great benefit; hence, it is 'directly visible' (sandiṭṭhiko). In this way, the remaining passages should be applied and explained accordingly. But the meaning of the words should be understood according to the method explained in the expositions on the Visuddhimagga (Visuddhi. Mahāṭī. 1.147). The fourth is clear in meaning.

Aññatarabrāhmaṇasuttādivaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Aññatarabrāhmaṇa Sutta and others is concluded.

5. Nibbutasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Nibbuta Sutta

56. Pañcame na kālantare pattabbanti yadā saccappaṭivedho, tadā eva laddhabbattā na kālantare pattabbaṃ. Maggañāṇena upanetabbattā upaneyyaṃ. Upaneyyameva opaneyyikanti āha “paṭipattiyā upagantabba”nti.

56. In the fifth, "not to be attained at a later time" means that because it is to be obtained at the very time when there is penetration of the truth, it is not to be attained at a later time. "To be brought near" (upaneyyaṃ) is so called because it is to be brought near by the knowledge of the path. "Leading onward" (opaneyyika) means precisely "to be brought near;" thus he said, "it is to be approached by practice."

Nibbutasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Nibbuta Sutta is concluded.

6. Palokasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Paloka Sutta

57. Chaṭṭhe ācariyapācariyānanti ācariyānampi ācariyānaṃ. Nirantaraphuṭo nerayikasattehi nirayagāmikammassa kārakānaṃ bahubhāvā. Ubhayampetanti yathāvuttaṃ atthadvayaṃ. Ghananivāsatanti gāmānaṃ ghanasannivāsataṃ. Ekanteneva adhammoti ayonisomanasikārahetukattā anatthahetutāya ca niyameneva adhammo. Na adhammarāgoti adhippetoti paraparikkhāresu rāgo viya na mahāsāvajjoti katvā vuttaṃ. Tathā hi sakasakaparikkhāravisayo rāgo visamalobho viya na ekantato apāyuppattijanako. Paraparikkhāresu uppajjamānassa mahāsāvajjatāya adhammarāgatā. Lobhassa samakālo nāma natthi kāyaduccaritādīnaṃ viya ayonisomanasikārasamuṭṭhānattā. Esāti eso pāpadhammo. Samalobho visamalakkhaṇābhāvato. Tathā hi taṃsamuṭṭhāno payogo micchācāroti [M 2.0129] na vuccati. Avatthupaṭisevanasaṅkhātenāti yaṃ lokiyasādhusamanuññātaṃ rāgassa vatthuṭṭhānaṃ, tato aññasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ paṭisevanasaṅkhātena.

57. In the sixth, 'of teachers and teachers of teachers' means of the teachers of even the teachers. The hell is continuously pervaded by hell-beings due to the abundance of those who commit actions leading to hell. 'Both' refers to the two meanings as previously explained. 'Dense habitation' means the dense settlement of villages. 'Entirely unrighteous'—because it has unwise attention as its cause and is a cause of harm, it is invariably unrighteous. 'Not unrighteous lust' is intended to mean that, unlike lust for the possessions of others, it is not said to be highly blameworthy. For lust directed toward one's own possessions, unlike improper greed (visamalobha), does not absolutely lead to arising in a lower realm. Because lust arising for the possessions of others is highly blameworthy, it is unrighteous lust. For greed, there is no such thing as a proper occasion, as there might be for bodily misconduct and so on, because it arises from unwise attention. 'This' refers to this evil state. 'Balanced greed' (samalobho) is so called because it lacks the characteristic of imbalance. For the action arising from it is not called wrong conduct. 'By the description of engaging in an improper object' refers to engaging in an object other than that which is approved by good worldly people as a basis for lust.

Vividhasassānanti [V 2.0119] sālivīhiādinānappakārasassānaṃ. Dussassanti paccayadūsena dūsitaṃ sassaṃ. Sampajjamāneti nipphajjanato pageva gabbhaparivuddhikāle. Pāṇakāti salabhādipāṇakā. Patantīti sassānaṃ matthake patanti. Salākāmattameva sampajjatīti vaḍḍhitvā gabbhaṃ gahetuṃ asamatthaṃ sampajjati. Teti vāḷaamanussā. Laddhokāsāti yakkhādhipatīhi anuññātattā laddhokāsā.

'Various crops' means crops of various kinds, such as fine rice, paddy, and so on. 'Blighted crops' means a crop ruined by unfavorable conditions. 'When they are ripening' means even before they are produced, at the time of the embryo's growth. 'Insects' means insects such as locusts and other pests. 'Fall' means they fall upon the tops of the crops. 'Only a mere stalk remains' means having grown, it becomes unable to develop a seed-bud. 'They' are wild animals and non-human beings. 'Having gained opportunity' means having gained the opportunity because they are permitted by the lords of the yakkhas.

Palokasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Paloka Sutta is concluded.

7. Vacchagottasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Vacchagotta Sutta

58. Sattame mahāvipākanti uḷāraphalaṃ bahuvipākaṃ. Dhammo nāma kathitakathā “atthaṃ dahati vidahatī”ti katvā. Anudhammo nāma paṭikathanaṃ “taṃ anugato dhammo”ti katvā. Saha dhammenāti sahadhammo, so eva sahadhammiko. Dhammasaddo cettha kāraṇapariyāyoti āha “sakāraṇo”ti. Vādassāti vacanassa. Anupāto anupacchā pavatti.

58. In the seventh, 'greatly fruitful' means yielding abundant and significant results. 'Dhamma' refers to the discourse, so called because it holds meaning and destroys defilements. 'Anudhammo' refers to the responsive discourse, so called because it is the Dhamma that conforms to it. 'With the dhamma' means 'accompanied by the dhamma,' hence 'one who shares the same dhamma.' Here, the term 'dhamma' is used in the sense of a reason, as stated: 'with a reason.' 'Of speech' means of verbal expression. 'Continuity' means the uninterrupted flow.

Paripanthe tiṭṭhatīti pāripanthiko. Panthe ṭhatvā paresaṃ sāpateyyaṃ chindanato panthadūhanacoro. Yadi paccavekkhaṇañāṇaṃ, kathaṃ taṃ asekkhanti āha “asekkhassa pavattattā”ti. Itarānīti sīlakkhandhādīni. Sayampīti pi-saddo “asekkhassa pavattā cā”ti imamatthaṃ sampiṇḍeti.

'One who stands in the way' is an obstructor. A 'highway robber' is a thief who, standing on the path, robs others of their possessions. If it is the knowledge of reviewing, how is it the knowledge of one beyond training? It is said: 'because it occurs in one beyond training.' 'The others' refers to the aggregates beginning with virtue. Regarding 'sayampi', the particle 'pi' combines this meaning: 'and it occurs for one beyond training.'

Nibbisevanoti visevanarahito vigatavilomabhāvo. Na upaparikkhantīti na vicārenti. Jātiṃ nibbattiṃ yāti upagacchatīti jātiyo, jātoti attho. Tenāha “yattha katthaci kulajāte”ti.

'Not indulging' means devoid of indulgence, free from opposition. 'They do not investigate' means they do not reflect. 'Jātiyo' means one who goes to birth, approaches arising; the meaning is 'born'. Hence it is said: 'born in whatever family.'
